question: The Bhavani improved from Priority IV to V - did the Rs 428 crore plan do it, or was the stretch marginal all along?
intro: The good-news stretch, with an attribution question. The 2019 action plan's own baseline sampling found 18 of 19 river stations already meeting bathing criteria - the pollution case rested on a few failing sewage drains at Sirumugai and the untreated outfalls of Mettupalayam and Erode. Against that, six towns committed roughly Rs 428 crore of sewerage works. CPCB moved the stretch from Priority IV (2018) to V (2022, 2025), and TNPCB's 2023 readings ran Class A-B all year. Which of the committed works actually exist - and would the numbers look different without them?

primary.label: TNPCB stretch-wise monthly water-quality reports
primary.note: December 2023 is the last stretch-wise edition TNPCB published. All Bhavani stations ran Class A-B through 2023; even the plan-era MINARS series (2011-2018) never showed BOD above 3 mg/L at the stretch stations.

actionPlan.label: TNPCB Action Plan on Rejuvenation of River Bhavani, Sirumugai to Kalingarayan (Sept 2019)

baseline.banner: Tamil Nadu publishes no stretch-wise infrastructure progress report - completion status below is reconstructed from public scheme lists and municipal pages, and 'no completion record found' is a finding about reporting, not necessarily about the work.
otherSources: CPCB Polluted River Stretches reports: 2018 (Priority IV, Sirumugai to Kalingarayan) - 2022 (Priority V, along Bhavani, BOD 4.6) - October 2025 (Priority V, single location at Sirumugai, BOD 3.3; mirrored on this site)

Plan Annexure-I industrial effluent record, Jan-Oct 2018: several paper-mill and sugar-unit exceedances (BOD up to 100, COD up to 640 mg/L) sit in the annexure despite the plan's 'no industrial discharge' narrative

plan-record.label: TNPCB Bhavani action plan (Sept 2019) - commitments, outfall GPS register (27 outfalls), baseline sampling
CPCB action-plan approval minutes for the Bhavani

regions.name: Erode City Municipal Corporation
regions.inBasinNote: 5.5 lakh people; 44 MLD sewage, ~5 MLD via the Konavaikkal drain into the Kalingarayan Canal; the Vairapalayam dump yard sits on the Cauvery's right bank. Erode's reach spans the canal and the Cauvery confluence at the stretch's tail.

categories.label: Public STPs & sewer network

actionPlan.summary: UGSS at Rs 209.22 crore with a 50.55 MLD STP at Vendipalayam ('ready for commissioning' at plan time); 7,274 of 72,500 house connections done, the rest committed by December 2019, after which 'outfalls will be stopped permanently'.

mpr.summary: No public completion record found for the remaining ~65,000 connections or full STP utilisation. The Salem pattern - plant ready, network unfinished - is the open question here too, with no published number since 2019.

gaps: House-connection count was 10% at plan time with a 3-month deadline; no later figure has been published anywhere we can find.

actionPlan.summary: Bio-mining of the Vairapalayam dump yard on the Cauvery's bank (~140 TPD accumulating): commence May 2019, complete March 2020, Smart City funding. Plus 24 micro-composting centres (70 TPD) by August-October 2019.

mpr.summary: No completion record found for the biomining of the riverbank dump - the single largest physical commitment on the Cauvery's bank in this plan.

regions.name: Mettupalayam Municipality & Sirumugai Town Panchayat
regions.inBasinNote: The stretch's head. Mettupalayam: ~80,000 people, ~7-8 MLD untreated via three drains, 8 km upstream of the notified stretch. Sirumugai: the town whose failing drains (BOD 153 at the Muniappan temple drain) were the plan's clearest pollution evidence - and the location CPCB still flags in 2025.

categories.label: Sewage treatment

actionPlan.summary: Mettupalayam: UGSS at Rs 91.70 crore with an 8.65 MLD STP and 17,000 connections, target June 2020 (another page of the same plan says 2021). Sirumugai: Rs 2 crore sullage scheme by 'Nano Bio Ozolyte Technology', target June 2020.

mpr.summary: No commissioning record found for either. CPCB's October 2025 assessment still lists its Bhavani polluted location at Sirumugai - the same town whose drains were the 2019 evidence - suggesting the head-of-stretch interception is at best incomplete.

gaps: The plan itself carries two different Mettupalayam completion dates (June 2020 and 2021).
'Nano Bio Ozolyte' appears in no public procurement or commissioning record we can find.

regions.name: Sathyamangalam & Gobichettipalayam Municipalities
regions.inBasinNote: Mid-stretch towns: Sathyamangalam 38,000 people / 5 mapped outfalls; Gobichettipalayam 64,000 / sullage to the Keeripalam odai.

actionPlan.summary: Sathyamangalam: UGSS at Rs 54.26 crore with two STPs (5.38 MLD), completion December 2019, 7,200 connections. Gobichettipalayam: 20 KLD FSTP (Rs 2.5 crore) by December 2019; Keeripalam odai rejuvenation (Rs 55.2 crore) and a 5 MLD STP on the Thadapalli canal (Rs 12.41 crore, NABARD) by December 2020.

mpr.summary: No completion record found for any of the five works. Sathyamangalam's 4 MLD STP at Kottuveerampalayam was 'under construction' in 2019 with a consent that had lapsed schedule-wise; nothing later is public.

regions.name: Industry on the stretch (paper, sugar, distillery, dyeing)
regions.inBasinNote: 737 units inspected: 12 paper mills (Sathyamangalam), 2 sugar + 2 distillery majors (Appakudal/Chinnapuliyur, OCEMS-equipped), 49-51 dyeing units on ZLD (Bhavani taluk), 4 large ZLD textile units upstream at Mettupalayam.

categories.label: Industrial effluent

actionPlan.summary: The action table's industrial row says 'No industrial discharge' with no timeline. Yet the plan's own Annexure-I (Jan-Oct 2018 monitoring) records paper-mill BOD up to 50 and COD up to 640 mg/L, and a sugar-unit BOD of 100 - and the plan's enforcement section admits night-hour illegal discharge into the Kalingarayan Canal by consented ZLD units, policed by power disconnection and sealing.

mpr.summary: No public follow-up reconciles the annexure's exceedances or the night-discharge enforcement with the 'no industrial discharge' claim; the suggested online water-quality monitors at four river locations were never timelined and have no public trace.

gaps: The plan proposes OCWQMS at Bhavanisagar, Sathyamangalam, Appakudal and Kalingarayan Dam - a directly checkable commitment with no completion record.

regions.name: Town & village panchayats on the stretch (Bhavanisagar, Urachikottai, Punjai Pugalur and others)
regions.inBasinNote: Bhavanisagar TP: 3 GPS-mapped outfalls, Rs 60 lakh sullage scheme. Urachikottai VP: 1,416 individual + 27 community soak pits committed under MGNREGS by June 2021.

actionPlan.summary: Bhavanisagar: Nano Bio Ozolyte sullage scheme (Rs 60 lakh, IUDM) by June 2020 plus a compost-yard compound wall (Rs 36 lakh) by May 2019. Urachikottai: 1,416 individual and 27 community soak pits under MGNREGS 2019-21 by June 2021 (42 already built).

mpr.summary: No completion record found in any public source.
